# Krishna Book Bedtime

## Story 021 — The Stealing of the Boys and Calves by Brahma

## Main Story
The morning in Vṛndāvana shone bright as ever, the grass glistening with tiny drops of dew under the feet of the boys and their frolicking calves. Kṛṣṇa’s eyes sparkled with joy as He led His friends deeper into the green forest with baskets of rice and sweet fruits from home.

Soon they found a soft shady spot under tall trees, and the air was full of music from birds and the soft lowing of calves settling nearby. But as everyone enjoyed their meal, someone high above watched closely—it was Lord Brahmā, the great creator in the universe.

Brahmā decided to test the Lord, and with mystic power he hid the calves and then the cowherd boys in a secret cave of his own making. When Kṛṣṇa returned, He called softly for the calves, but they were hidden by Brahmā’s spell and could not answer.

Seeing that neither His friends nor the calves were anywhere to be found, He realized that mighty Brahmā was behind this illusion. To protect the cowherd boys and their families from sadness, and to teach Brahmā about His power, Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself into exact forms of all the missing calves and boys.

He copied them perfectly, right down to their laughter, their voices, how they walked, and all their playful habits. After a year had passed for Brahmā, he returned and was astonished to see the same boys and calves still playing with Kṛṣṇa.

Before Brahmā’s astonished gaze, each expanded form turned into a shining four-armed Viṣṇu form filled with divine light. Overwhelmed with awe and respect, Brahmā offered his humble prayers to Lord Kṛṣṇa and understood the greatness and loving kindness of the Lord.
